dedupe_keys.name: ida s climate response 2045 how denmark can become climate neutral in energy and transport energyplan scenario with model files

description: IDA's Climate Response 2045 is a national scenario by the Danish Society of Engineers and the Sustainable Energy Planning Research Group at Aalborg University for a climate-neutral Danish energy and transport system by 2045, modelled with the EnergyPLAN hourly energy system model. The case study page read on 2026-09-28 links the Danish report, an English summary and a zip of the EnergyPLAN model files. It was published in May 2020 and in June 2021 with modelling of 2045, and it concludes that wind power must grow from about 6 GW in 2020 to 11 GW in 2030 and 19 GW in 2045, solar power to 5 and 10 GW, electrolysis to 1,200 and 4,800 MW, district heating to 63 percent of heat demand with surplus heat from industry, data centres and electrofuels, and that cars, buses and a share of lorries must be electric, with 400 km of electric roads by 2045. Coverage is Denmark. Access is free; no licence is stated for the model files. Caveats: it is an advocacy scenario, and industry, agriculture and waste are outside its scope. It supports capacity planning studies of highly renewable systems by giving ready input files. Related record: the EnergyPLAN model itself.

name: IDA's Climate Response 2045: how Denmark can become climate neutral in energy and transport (EnergyPLAN scenario with model files)
outcomes: A route to 70% emission cuts by 2030 and climate neutrality in energy and transport by 2045: wind from about 6 GW (2020) to 11 GW (2030) and 19 GW (2045), solar PV to 5 and 10 GW, 1,200 and 4,800 MW of electrolysis, district heating to 63% of heat demand, CCU before CCS, electrified cars and buses and 400 km of e-roads by 2045.
provider: Danish Society of Engineers (IDA) with the Sustainable Energy Planning Research Group, Aalborg University
resources_used: Danish energy and transport demand and supply data

sources.note: read: authors Lund, Mathiesen, Thellufsen, Sorknæs, Ridjan Skov; links to Danish report, English summary and EnergyPLAN model files (IDA2045.zip); scenario for climate neutrality by 2045 in energy and transport; published May 2020 and June 2021 with modelling of 2045; conclusions: heat savings 12% by 2030 and 30% by 2045, wind 6 GW to 11 GW (2030) and 19 GW (2045), PV 1 GW to 5 GW and 10 GW, electrolysis 1,200 MW and 4,800 MW, district heating to 63% of heat demand, CCU priority, biomass conversion, electric cars and 35% battery lorries and 400 km e-roads by 2045
